newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Airways pilots call strike.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Airways pilots call strike.

text.p: National carrier Kenya Airways said on Thursday it would cancel all flights for a second day following a strike called by pilots to protest against the suspension of two of their colleagues.

"Kenya Airways regrets to announce that the pilots' union, KALPA, gave an ultimatum to the company on Wednesday that unless it withdrew the suspension of two pilots, the union would institute strike action," airline spokesman Koome Mwambia said.
"Two pilots have been suspended on full pay pending an enquiry which may, or may not, lead to disciplinary action depending on the outcome," Mwambia added in a statement.

Mwambia said Kenya Airways had informed the pilots' union that the strike action was in contravention of Kenya's trade dispute laws that made it a criminal offence to strike without notice in an essential service.

"After the declaration of the strike on Wednesday, eight pilots reported sick, leading to the cancellation of (domestic) flights to Mombasa, Kisumu (and international flights to) Lilongwe, Lusaka and Dubai," Mwambia said. "It is expected that further flights will be cancelled on Thursday."
Mwambia said approximately 300 passengers were affected on the first day of the strike on Wednesday but attempts were being made to find alternative flights for them.
Kenya Airways employs some 110 pilots, Mwambia said.
The government sold 51 percent of its shareholding in the airline on the Nairobi Stock Exchange early this year.
That followed a government sale of a 26 percent stake in the airline to KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV. The stock was first traded on June 3.

Disputes between the airline and management and pilots have undermined the Kenya Airways share for some time now. From a flotation price of 11.25 shillings, it closed at 9.90 on Wednesday -- before news of the strike hit the market.
In July, a court awarded the pilots around 411 million shillings representing two years back pay after they complained they were some of the poorest paid pilots on the globe.
